registryLegalName: Solicitor Application to Destroy Arrest Records After Successful Alcohol Education Program Completion, S.C. Code § 17-22-530(A)

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: On successful completion of an alcohol education programme the circuit solicitor shall effect a noncriminal disposition of the alcohol-related offence, and no record may be maintained except by the Commission on Prosecution Coordination to prevent a second use.
Following the noncriminal disposition the person may apply to the court for an order to destroy all official records relating to the arrest.

Eligibility is confined to a person at least seventeen but under twenty-one at the time of arrest, with no prior alcohol-related offence and no significant history of prior delinquency or criminal activity, charged with one of eleven enumerated offences or another offence similar in nature and severity as determined by the circuit solicitor. Participation is once only.
Each circuit solicitor has prosecutorial discretion to establish the alcohol education programme, which is under the solicitor's direct supervision and control.
Names the alcohol education program director as an attestor for the expungement paperwork.
Subsection (E)(1) exempts § 17-22-530(A) from the SLED verification fee.

counselFlags: South Carolina expungements start with either the Solicitor's Office or the summary court and use the official SCCA 223-series forms. LegalEase must not produce a substitute for an official South Carolina Judicial Branch form.
South Carolina generally expunges one charge per order, with special fee-treatment rules for related charges arising from the same incident under the Uniform Expungement Act.

A pardon is a separate process through the Department of Probation, Parole and Pardon Services and is NOT expungement. Do not file a pardon as an expungement and do not tell a participant that a pardon clears the record.
Waiting period: none beyond successful completion of the alcohol education programme and the circuit solicitor's noncriminal disposition under § 17-22-530(A).

Court level not settled: § 17-22-530(B) refers to 'the court' without naming a level, and the source does not settle whether the application runs through general sessions or summary court. Determine the court level and disposition first; no court is named by LegalEase.
No verification or notarization statute is identified for the § 17-22-530(B) application. Verification is a feature of the official SCCA form, which is not drafted here; nothing is filled.

Eligibility is narrow and age-bound: at least seventeen but under twenty-one at the time of arrest, no prior alcohol-related offence, no significant history of prior delinquency or criminal activity, and one of the eleven enumerated offences. Participation is once only.
DUI offences under §§ 56-5-2930 and 56-5-2933 are expressly excluded by § 17-22-520(C)(11).
Whether an offence is 'similar in nature and severity' to the eleven enumerated offences is a determination reserved to the circuit solicitor. LegalEase must never make or predict that determination.

Fees at source: the Alcohol Education Program carries a $250 programme fee plus possible provider fees; inability to pay cannot bar participation, and the solicitor may waive or reduce fees. The SLED verification fee is not charged for this route.

Attestation: § 17-22-940(D) names the alcohol education program director as an attestor. That attestation is obtained from the programme, and LegalEase never attests completion or asserts that it occurred.

waitingPeriods.duration: None beyond successful completion and the solicitor's noncriminal disposition under § 17-22-530(A).

exclusions: Any person under seventeen or twenty-one or older at the time of arrest.
Any person with a prior alcohol-related offence, or a significant history of prior delinquency or criminal activity.
Any second participation; § 17-22-520(B) allows the programme only once.
Driving under the influence offences under §§ 56-5-2930 and 56-5-2933, which § 17-22-520(C)(11) expressly excludes.
Any offence outside the eleven enumerated in § 17-22-520(C) unless the circuit solicitor determines it similar in nature and severity.
Any participant who violated the conditions and was terminated, in which case the offence is reinstated.
